title: End-to-end scenario demonstration (synthetic data)
notice: All accounts and transfers are synthetic (forensic scenario generator). Ground truth was used only to choose examples and to score the output; the engine never received it. Results describe behaviour on this synthetic ledger and say nothing about real-world accuracy.

summary.name: Multiple affected accounts
summary.aggregate: 18/21 victims detected; 9/21 surfaced >= 1 other victim (20/46 other victims found)

summary.name: Innocent counterparty
summary.aggregate: 21/22 innocent counterparties appeared; 0/22 labelled intermediary/suspicious; 0/22 given restriction review

summary.name: Potential secondary victim
summary.aggregate: 2/4 labelled victim-class and not intermediary (new criterion); 0/4 labelled exactly potential secondary victim (old criterion); 0/4 labelled intermediary/suspicious; 0/4 given restriction review

onward_attribution_conflicts.description: Accounts labelled intermediary/suspicious on pass-through (ONWARD) evidence although their traced onward transfers were at least twice the traced money they received and the engine's own balance-based attribution lower bound is 0: the onward money was mostly the account's own.

scenario_6_criterion_change.new_criterion: role_candidate is victim-class (potential_secondary_victim, or suspicious_activity_victim_unconfirmed with may_be_victim true) AND role_candidate is not potential_intermediary / potentially_suspicious_account
scenario_6_criterion_change.new_criterion_status: exploratory only; not used for pass/fail
scenario_6_criterion_change.reason: The owner's requirement is that the system distinguishes potential victim status from intermediary status, not that it uses one particular role name. The criterion was changed AFTER observing the result: the engine now labels FS-29869761 as an unconfirmed victim (suspicious_activity_victim_unconfirmed, may_be_victim true) because its balance-based attribution cannot show that the traced money itself moved on, so the 'passed traced money on' part of the secondary-victim rule is not supported. The scenario is scored with the ORIGINAL criterion; the revised one is an exploratory metric only, validated separately on the untouched hold-out ledger.

criterion_change.new_criterion: role_candidate is victim-class (potential_secondary_victim, or suspicious_activity_victim_unconfirmed with may_be_victim true) AND role_candidate is not potential_intermediary / potentially_suspicious_account
criterion_change.new_criterion_status: exploratory only; not used for pass/fail
criterion_change.reason: The owner's requirement is that the system distinguishes potential victim status from intermediary status, not that it uses one particular role name. The criterion was changed AFTER observing the result: the engine now labels FS-29869761 as an unconfirmed victim (suspicious_activity_victim_unconfirmed, may_be_victim true) because its balance-based attribution cannot show that the traced money itself moved on, so the 'passed traced money on' part of the secondary-victim rule is not supported. The scenario is scored with the ORIGINAL criterion; the revised one is an exploratory metric only, validated separately on the untouched hold-out ledger.

scenarios.name: Previously unseen account IDs
scenarios.expected_behaviour: Investigated IDs never occur in training data, yet receive model scores.
scenarios.selection_rule: The investigated accounts of scenarios 1-6, compared with every account ID in data/v3_forensic/train (accounts.csv and both transaction ID columns).

scenarios.name: Normal legitimate accounts
scenarios.expected_behaviour: Ordinary accounts with enough history mostly show no suspicious activity; false flags reported.
scenarios.selection_rule: First 30 accounts (sorted by ID) labelled ordinary, in no scenario, with >= 10 transfers.
uncertain_or_missed: 1 ordinary account(s) returned insufficient_evidence: FS-01C0C988.
